commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to codebase
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding assertions reduces programmer mistakes, especially so when the codebase evolves.

As a step towards this goal, I've added a few assertions to ensure that user input is well-parsed,
the todolist is well-formed and indexing to the todolist is safe and quu is always constructed before window in GUI is shown

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #1 from Cookiemunchrr/branch-A-Assertions
TaskList: Extract index check and conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
removeTask, markTask and unmarkTask each repeat the same bounds check
and the same subtraction that turns the number the user types into the
position that number occupies in the backing list. The subtraction in
particular is a single fact about how the two numbering schemes relate,
yet it is stated in three places, so any change to the numbering shown
to the user would have to be found and made three times.

Move both the check and the conversion into one private helper. The
helper returns the converted index rather than only validating its
argument, because returning it absorbs the second repetition as well; a
validate-only helper would have left the subtraction behind in all
three callers.

Rename the parameter of the helper and of the three public methods to
taskNumber, reserving index for a position in the backing list. The two
kinds of number were both called index, and confusing them is the most
likely bug this class can have, so they should not share a word.
getTaskAt keeps index because it really does take one.

markTask and unmarkTask are still near-identical, differing only in
which Task method they call. That is left alone for now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Quu: Extract shared handling of add commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The todo, deadline and event branches of executeCommand are identical
apart from which parser method builds the task. All three record the
command category, add the task to the list and format the same
confirmation, so a fourth task type would mean copying those steps
again and thereafter keeping four copies in step.

Move the shared steps into handleAdd, which takes an already-built
Task. The parsing stays in the switch because that is where the
branching on the command word already happens. Parsing inside the
handler instead would force it to ask which kind of task it had been
given, recreating the same branch one level down and leaving two
places to update rather than one.

The other branches are left inline. What they need is a separate
change: they do not duplicate one another, so the reason to give them
a handler each is readability rather than reuse, and that is better
judged on its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Quu: Give each command its own handler
commitResults.messageBody:
executeCommand answers two questions at once. The switch labels answer
which command the user typed, while the statements inside each branch
answer how it is carried out, parsing the argument, updating the task
list and formatting the reply. A reader who wants only the list of
commands Quu supports has to read all forty-odd lines to find it.

Move the body of each branch into a handler named after its command,
leaving the switch as a mapping from a command word to a single call.
The two-line branches, list and find, are extracted along with the
rest even though neither is long. The aim is not to shorten individual
branches but to leave every arm of the switch at the same level, since
one arm still describing how it works would drop the reader an
altitude for a single line.

Use the arrow form of switch now that no branch declares a local. The
colon form shares one scope across every label, which is why six
branches needed braces purely to reuse the name task; those braces
described the language rather than the logic. The arrow form also
cannot fall through, so a missing break is no longer a bug that can be
written.

The handlers take QuuException rather than each listing the specific
exceptions it can raise. They are private and the public methods still
document the individual failures, so the shorter signature was
preferred over the more precise one.

Behaviour is unchanged. The handlers hold the same statements in the
same order, the tests pass, and a manual run of all eight commands and
of the unknown-command, bad-index and missing-argument paths produces
the same output as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace command category strings with an enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Quu records the category of each reply in a String field, taken from
eight String constants, and DialogBox switches on string literals to
pick a style class for it. Nothing ties the two sides together. Change
the value of COMMAND_ADD from "add" to anything else and the code
still compiles, the tests still pass, and the GUI quietly stops
colouring replies to add commands because its switch falls through to
default. The two files sit in different packages and are held in
agreement only by matching text.

Introduce CommandType and use it for the field, for the accessor and
for the parameter DialogBox receives, so a category that does not
exist can no longer be written or compared against.

The enum names reply categories rather than command words. That is why
it has one ADD constant covering the todo, deadline and event
commands, which are three things to type but one thing to look at, and
why the command words themselves stay as the strings they are matched
against. EXIT_COMMAND likewise stays a String: it is compared against
what the user typed, which an enum constant cannot be.

Make the switch in DialogBox an expression rather than a statement. An
enum switch statement need not be exhaustive, so a new category could
be added and silently left unstyled, whereas a switch expression must
cover every constant. Adding one to CommandType now fails to compile
until it is given a style, which was the reason for preferring an enum
over constants in the first place.

Behaviour is unchanged. The categories map one to one onto the strings
they replace, and a run covering every command, the failure paths and
the exit path produces the same output as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Split readFile into one step per line
commitResults.messageBody:
readFile nests a switch inside a try inside a while, and the body of
that loop does five separate things: skip blank lines, split a line
into fields, check it has enough of them, build a task of the right
kind, and apply the done flag. Reading it means holding all five in
mind at once while three levels of indentation obscure which of them
each statement belongs to.

The message reporting a bad line is also built three times, once for
each way a line can fail. Wanting to add the line number to it, say,
would mean finding and editing all three identically.

Give the loop a single step, parseLine, which takes one line and
returns the task it describes, and let that in turn use createTask and
applyDoneFlag. The seam is the one the file format already implies:
one line holds one task. Cutting there removes the nesting rather than
hiding it, because the switch and the try move out of the loop instead
of moving into a helper called from it.

Build the corruption message in corruptedLine, and have it return the
exception rather than throw it, so that every caller still writes the
throw keyword. A helper that threw would leave each call site looking
like an ordinary call that returns, and the compiler treating the code
after it as reachable.

createTask raises the QuuException a task raises rather than an
InvalidFileContents. Only the caller knows which line the fields came
from, so only the caller can describe the failure in terms of the
file.

Behaviour is unchanged, and checking that needed more than the tests:
the only test of readFile round trips a valid file, whereas nearly all
of this method is error handling. Running both versions over a line
with too few fields, an unknown type, a done flag that is neither 0
nor 1, details that do not fit the type, and an event ending before it
starts produces identical output in every case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop exposing the list backing TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList guards how tasks are reached. Positions are checked before
use, and the numbering the user types is converted in one place. None
of that holds, because getTodoList hands out the live backing list.
Any caller can add, remove or clear through it and reach the tasks
without passing a single one of those checks.

The getter exists for one reason: so Storage can walk the tasks and
write them out. Writing them needs to read the tasks, not to
restructure them, so the access granted is far wider than the need.
The constructor leaves the same hole facing the other way, keeping the
list it is passed rather than copying it, so the caller retains a
reference to what is now this object's state.

Give writeFile a TaskList and let it read through getSize and
getTaskAt, then delete the getter and copy the list the constructor
receives. Deleting the getter is preferred over returning an
unmodifiable view of it, because a view still offers the methods and
fails only when one is called. With no getter at all, reaching the
list fails to compile.

This also settles an asymmetry in Storage, which returned a TaskList
from readFile but took a List from writeFile, even though the two are
opposite halves of the same job.

The cost is that writeFile now counts through the tasks by index
instead of using a for-each. That is accepted here rather than making
TaskList iterable, which would mean handing out an Iterator and with
it a remove method, reopening a narrower version of the same hole.

Verified by adding, marking and listing tasks through the running
program and confirming the save file matches, plus the existing round
trip test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
